obligation: FD&C Act section 524B, cyber device requirements
basis: The company plans a 510(k) for WM-1, which includes firmware, connects to the internet through Wi-Fi, BLE and the cloud service, and could be vulnerable to cybersecurity threats, so it meets all three parts of the cyber device definition in 524B(c). No size exemption; no device exemption under 524B(d) identified

obligation: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR), incorporating ISO 13485 by reference
basis: The company designs the finished device and develops its specifications (820.1(a); 820.3 manufacturer). Design controls apply to class II devices (820.10(c)). Production is outsourced to a contract manufacturer under a quality agreement, which does not move these duties
Duties start when WM-1 is in commercial distribution; no device is marketed today. The procedure must exist before launch
807.20(a)(1) covers a person who develops specifications for a device made by a second party. Timing to be confirmed by the regulatory consultant

obligation: FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance (issued 2026-02-03) and postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016)
basis: FDA uses the guidance to judge whether a 524B submission shows reasonable assurance of cybersecurity

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
basis: No defense contracts; receipts come mainly from a hospital system's development and evaluation agreement

obligation: CMMC Program rule and DFARS CMMC acquisition rule

basis: No defense articles or defense work

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule and breach notice as a business associate
citation: 45 CFR 160.103; 45 CFR Part 164, Subparts C and D
basis: The company holds no PHI: the cloud service holds simulator and test data, and no patient is connected to any unit.
